pr_title: Limit fronius error messages on failed connection
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Fronius devices are often powered only by self-produced solar power.
They therefore turn off at night, resulting in connection errors.
This currently spams the home assistant log at a rate of 1/scan_interval.
As requested in #42046 it would already be a big help if the sensor only once logs an error about failed connection
and then keeps shut about it.

Even better would be to implement a system wide handler for sensors that exhibit connection errors when the target device is turned off (i.e. also for printers)

I am not sure whether this is the preferred way of handling such issues. Please let me know if there are any official guidelines about this.

pr_comments: It would be good to implement the entity `available` property and update that depending on connection state.

Adding to this, the entity could implement the should_poll property. However I could not find documentation on how home assistant ensures regular calling of the async_update method - currently this is implemented by manually creating a lambda service. Is there a home assistant standard for this (i.e. directly following scan_interval)? Would the change be significant (wrt necessary code changes)? (see "async_track_time_interval" in the platform setup)

The integration should preferably be refactored to use our coordinator update helper and a discovery function that adds new entities that is connected to the coordinator via our dispatch helper.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/integration_fetching_data#coordinated-single-api-poll-for-data-for-all-entities

One or many coordinators can be used.

Great, thanks for the pointer! However a full refactoring would be beyond the scope of this change, which is meant as a quick patch to fix #42046. I can make the refactoring of this entity and the related `syncthru` entity by me a new issue and will handle it as time permits.

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
I have the fronius sensor running in my setup. The fronius inverter is powered directly from the solar panels, meaning during the night there is no power and the web interface of the inverted is not accessible. This throws HA off and creates a lot of error logs.

Is there a way for HA to recognize such situation and work properly?

The worst part is when HA instance is restarted when sensor is not responsive, as it also does not create corresponding entity:

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: v0.116.4
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): AFAIK it was always like that
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): container
- Integration causing this issue: fronius
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/fronius/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
sensors:
  - platform: fronius
    resource: http://fronius
    monitored_conditions:
      - sensor_type: inverter
        scope: system
      - sensor_type: inverter
        scope: device
        device: 1
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
2020-10-18 17:13:07 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.fronius.sensor] Failed to update: connection error
2020-10-18 17:14:04 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.fronius.sensor] Failed to update: connection error
2020-10-18 17:14:07 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.fronius.sensor] Failed to update: connection error
```

```
Entity not available: sensor.power_ac_fronius_inverter_1_http_fronius
```

## Additional information

Hi @mchwalisz ,

Sorry for the late reply!
not sure if I can do anything from the integration part - If the fronius device is not reachable, it might be due to a temporary shutdown or due to the provided url being incorrect. This holds for a number of devices (i.e. printers that are not always turned on). In my opinion there should be a home-assistant wide solution for this. 

A very hacky workaround could be to set up your home network (or the device running HA) to provide a backup page in case the fronius device is not reachable. Then, a static page (maybe with the latest data) could be provided instead.

PS: the keyword here is "fail-over" but I am not sure if this is easy  to set up in a local network (at least I found no simple guide by a quick search)

@nielstron that's exactly what is happening, because the inverter is only turned on when the sun is shining, and automatically shuts off for the night. I know that the error has to be reported, but couldn't it be reported only once, instead of repeating the same error log string 9999x time till the next morning?

@Gollam The fronius frontend allows nothing else but "local polling" and I guess that every time a poll occurs on the shut down device the error is printed.

One could of course locally store whether the connection already failed the last time and not print an error message in that case. Not sure if there is a development guideline about issues like this (IMO there should be one though, or a technical coverup). I can try to make this a merge request and see what the main staff of homeassistant sais about it

FWIW you can enable night mode from the front panel of the inverter which should prevent it powering down at night. I'm not sure if this is your exact issue or not.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ROJsbF402jA

Alternatively you can select `Logging during night-time hours: YES` in the `Fronius Solar Web` menu in the web interface, if you have admin access, and that will override night-time mode settings.
